finding: Non-Goal 6 defers the visibility of the discount and prices the deferral as a manual round-trip -- "until then an operator setting `blocking` reads the round files for what was suppressed" -- on the ground that the counterpart is pinned absent by six sites naming `nonblocking_open`. Counted against the code, that reason does not cover the cheapest route. All six pins name `nonblocking_open` on the record/status payload; none touches `tp audit --merge`, which the loop already runs on the same round before `--record` and which already computes a breakdown over the deduped rows: `audit_merge.go:61-86` builds `by_status` and `by_role` and emits `severity` nowhere (a search for `severity` in that file returns zero). So the one number that makes `blocking` readable -- how many non-PASS rows were discounted, by severity -- could be a single key on a summary map the agent already parses, strippable under `--compact` the way `overlap_report` at `:90-92` already is, inverting no pinned guard and adding no command, flag or new payload. The release instead ships its only feature with its effect unreadable and bills the operator for hand-reading NDJSON.
suggestion: Either name the merge summary as the answer -- a `by_severity` counter over non-PASS rows on `--merge`'s existing summary map, omitted under `--compact` like `overlap_report` -- and add it to §2's scope and a §5 test, or state in Non-Goal 6 why the merge summary is out of scope as well, since the six-pin argument that carries the deferral is about `nonblocking_open` on a different payload and does not reach it.

finding: The fence added this round says `tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=blocking` exits 2 under `TP_UNATTENDED=1` "with the escalation hint the other fenced decisions use", and §5 test 11 pins "the escalation hint". Neither says which decision name. That name is not free-form: `tp escalate --decision` is a closed, validated set -- `skip-gate, raise-review-cap, raise-audit-cap, import-force, other` (`internal/cli/escalate.go:41`, refused by `IsEscalationDecision` at `:82`) -- and `escalationDecision(field)` in `internal/cli/unattended.go:19-27` maps only `review_max_rounds` and `audit_max_rounds`, returning `other` for everything else. So as specified, a unit refused on this field escalates as `decision: other`, the run stops with `stop_reason: escalation`, and the record the driver hands the operator is byte-indistinguishable from every other unnamed escalation: the operator must read the free-text `evidence` on every stop to learn what the run stopped for, which is exactly the per-stop round-trip the named decisions exist to remove. The alternative -- a sixth decision name -- is new surface on a validated enum plus its hint string, and the release budgets neither. §5 test 11 passes under both readings, so the choice is not forced by any test.
suggestion: Decide it in §2: either state that `audit_converge_on` escalates under the existing `other` and say why an unnamed stop is acceptable for it, or name the sixth decision (e.g. `relax-audit-convergence`), add it to `engine.EscalationDecisions()` in this release's scope alongside the fence, and make §5 test 11 assert the decision name rather than "the escalation hint".

finding: The fence's route out is the most expensive round-trip tp has, and this release's own data says its answer is fixed before any run starts. §2 makes the field "opt-in, human-only", so under `tp run` a unit can never set it; the refusal points the unit at `tp escalate`, and an escalation is not a local cost -- it stops the whole run (`stop_reason: escalation`), burns the operator's turn, and needs a fresh `tp run` to resume. What the operator would be deciding is already decided in this file: §2.1 concludes `blocking` "would have shipped over an `error` row in 2 of 2 measured cycles" and calls that decisive, and §2 keeps the default at `all` on exactly that ground. So the hint teaches every unit stuck in a long audit phase -- which §1 says is the recurring case, three cycles across two projects -- to halt the run for a question whose answer §2.1 pre-computed as no. The field's value comes from an operator setting it before the run with the numbers in front of them, which the fence already permits and which needs no escalation at all.
suggestion: Say in §2 that `audit_converge_on` is set outside a run and is not a legitimate escalation subject, and make the refusal's hint say so -- refuse, name §2.1's measurement, and tell the unit to continue under the resolved value -- rather than reusing the escalate hint. If escalation is meant to be legitimate for it, say what evidence would justify the operator answering yes, since §2.1 as written rules it out.

finding: §2's new cost measurement puts "both `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md` and `skills/tp/SKILL.md`" in scope by filename and names no claim in either. Those two files are the bytes every agent loads every session, so a stale sentence there is not a documentation debt -- it is a wrong decision per agent per session, which is the most expensive unit of waste tp has. Three claims in them are falsified or made misleading by this release and none is named. (1) `SKILL.md:152-153`, inside the v0.32.0 scope lesson: "tp has no audit-side equivalent of `review_converge_on` yet" -- shipping the field makes it false, and the naive repair ("now it does") teaches every agent that `audit_converge_on` closes the scope divergence, which Non-Goal 1 explicitly says this release does not narrow. (2) `SKILL.md:145`: "`tp audit --record` counts every row whose `status` is not exactly `PASS` ... so parking a finding leaves the round's finding count, the role streak and `--status --check` exactly where they were" -- under `blocking` the `--status --check` half is false for a `warning` or `info` row. (3) `REFERENCE.md:476` documents `review_converge_on` with the parenthetical "audit never reads it", which stays true but is now half a pair. §2 enumerates its call sites (§3) and its pins (§4) precisely because two earlier enumerations were short; the doc surface gets a file count instead, and §5 has no test or acceptance over either file.
suggestion: Enumerate the doc claim sites the way §3 enumerates call sites: name `SKILL.md:152-157`, `SKILL.md:145`, `SKILL.md:371` and `REFERENCE.md:476` in §2 (or a §2.3), say for each what must be true after the release -- in particular that the v0.32.0 scope paragraph must keep saying the divergence is open, per Non-Goal 1 -- and give §5 an acceptance that names them, as §2 already does for the `CLAUDE.md` precedence chain it does name.
